ice.name: Ice within reach
ice.dataset: SWIM ice consistency, 0-1 m and 1-5 m (PSI)
ice.why: Water for propellant, air and crops.

low_elevation.name: Low ground
low_elevation.dataset: MOLA MEGDR elevation, 16 pixels per degree (NASA PDS)
low_elevation.why: More atmosphere to slow the ship.
low_elevation.goodness_rule: 1 at -4,000 m or lower, 0 at +1,000 m or higher, linear between

plume_safe_ground.name: Plume-safe ground
plume_safe_ground.dataset: MGS TES nighttime thermal inertia, 20 pixels per degree (Putzig and Mellon, PSI)
plume_safe_ground.why: Firm soil the engines will not dig out: very low inertia is loose dust, very high is rock and bedrock.

science_reach.name: Science reach
science_reach.dataset: USGS Mars Global Geologic Map, SIM 3292 (Tanaka et al. 2014)
science_reach.why: More kinds of rock within a rover's range, and rock from the wet early eras.
science_reach.go: >= 4 distinct units within about 100 km, including a Noachian or Hesperian one
science_reach.goodness_rule: 0.7 x min(1, units / 6) + 0.3 x (1 if an old unit is within reach else 0)

magnetic_shelter.name: Magnetic shelter
magnetic_shelter.dataset: crustal magnetic field grid (not available in this run)
magnetic_shelter.why: Patches of magnetized crust add a little local radiation cover.

shown_not_scored.name: Regional slope
shown_not_scored.why: Flat, rock-free ground is SpaceX's own screen and needs HiRISE at landing scale; a 20 km slope is context, not a verdict.

shown_not_scored.name: Latitude
shown_not_scored.why: Sunlight and power are SpaceX's own screen (within about 40 degrees of the equator); we show it and leave it to them.

shown_not_scored.name: Dust (albedo)
shown_not_scored.why: Bright ground usually means a dust cover; thermal inertia already scores the firmness, so albedo stays context.
